clue.text: To crib and wail during mass

definitions.note: crib means home, so 'to crib' means towards home, an adverb

indicators.note: one thing happening during another sits within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a mass or stockpile of things is a hoard
to mew is to cry plaintively like a cat or gull

explanation.surface: A baby sobbing in church, or someone sneaking off to copy during a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crib' looks like copying or a cot, but here it is slang for home.
explanation.definitionFit: A crib is slang for a house, so going 'to crib' is heading towards one's dwelling.

clue.text: 'Pome' written on Cockney's locality (part of Bow)

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is written on top of the second

parts.note: a haw, the hawthorn's fruit, is a pome, an apple-like fruit
SE stands for south-east, the part of England (and London district) where Cockneys live

explanation.surface: A Cockney poem written about a spot in Bow, in east London.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is a district of east London, Cockney country, but here a bow is the front of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The hawse is the section of a ship's bows where the anchor cables pass through holes.

clue.text: Dude, go green!

parts.note: dude and man are both casual terms for a fellow
'get out!' is an order to go

explanation.surface: An exclamation urging a mate to become environmentally friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' looks like the environmental slogan but is a green vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: This flat pea pod, eaten whole, is a green vegetable.

clue.text: Why a new conception involves support for the distant past

indicators.note: involves means the anagram wraps round the support word
a conception is a fresh idea, so the letters are conceived anew in another order

parts.note: to back is to support

explanation.surface: Asking why a new idea relies on support from the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder; 'conception' is the signal, and 'involves' wraps the result round the support word.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an informal way of referring to a long-ago time.

clue.text: Set a puzzle full of holes

definitions.meaning: to riddle is to speak in or pose riddles
... means perforated, as in ... with bullets

explanation.surface: A setter makes a puzzle that has many flaws.
explanation.definitionFit: Posing a riddle is setting a puzzle; a target riddled with shots is perforated.

clue.text: Lustre of grand defeat

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds
a defeat is a loss

explanation.surface: The shine has gone off a great champion after a big defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloss is a surface shine, the same thing as a lustre.

clue.text: Almost objective state in which yoga is commonly practised

definitions.text: state in which yoga is commonly practised

indicators.note: almost means the word stops short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a goal is an objective

explanation.surface: Nearly reaching a goal of the state of mind yoga brings.
explanation.definitionFit: This Indian state on the west coast is famous for its beach retreats offering yoga.

clue.text: Round globe — seafarer encircles it

indicators.note: encircles it means the clue words go round the answer, which lies within them

explanation.surface: A sailor sails right round the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: Round as an adjective can mean plump or fat, which is what obese means.

clue.text: Special issue of magazine promotes subversive acts

indicators.note: promotes means the special letter is moved up to go ahead of the issue

parts.note: an edition is an issue of a magazine

explanation.surface: A magazine's special issue promotes subversion.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedition is conduct or speech inciting rebellion against the state.

clue.text: Tasteless items of jewellery? A couple mentioned in rap

parts.note: tat is cheap, tasteless goods, trinkets

indicators.note: mentioned means the couple's number is spoken aloud and spelt as heard

parts.note: a couple is two

explanation.surface: A rapper's tasteless bling, with a body-art pun for jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo is a rhythmic beating or tapping, as on a drum or door.

clue.text: Why to have information backed up off-line

indicators.note: the letter for why is set to have the reversed word before it, a charade joining
backed up means the word for information is read from back to front

parts.note: to be in the know is to have the information, so know serves as a noun for it
the letter Y is pronounced like the word why

explanation.surface: Asking why your files were backed up when the computer was off-line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off-line' suggests a disconnected computer, but here it means out of line, crooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Something out of alignment or not straight is crooked, askew, which is what wonky means.

clue.text: Cut flowers providing setting for start of anniversary at twelve o'clock

indicators.note: a setting holds a jewel, so the outer word holds the small piece within it

parts.note: to deadhead plants is to cut off their spent flowers

indicators.note: start of means only the opening letter of anniversary is taken

explanation.surface: A florist arranges cut flowers to mark the first anniversary of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut flowers' reads as a noun but is a gardening instruction, the verb deadhead.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve o'clock on a clock face is the pilot's way of saying straight in front.

clue.text: Pass by centre and stare

indicators.note: by means beside, so the two pieces sit next to each other

parts.note: the eye of a storm is its centre
in football a ball is a pass, as in 'a lovely ball through'

explanation.surface: A midfielder passes the ball by the centre circle, then stands staring.
explanation.definitionFit: To eyeball someone is to look at them hard and fixedly, a confrontational gaze.

clue.text: Storm off set, with stopgap taking lead part

indicators.note: taking lead part means the stopgap word plays the leading role, going first

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker, a stopgap

indicators.note: off means the letters of set are gone off, out of their order

explanation.surface: An actor storms off the film set while a stand-in takes the leading role.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest is a violent storm, especially one with high winds.

clue.text: Ponder incomplete bonus level of computer game

indicators.note: incomplete means the pondering word loses its final letter

parts.note: to mull over is to ponder
a tip is a gratuity, a bonus
a layer is a level

explanation.surface: Wondering about the bonus level of a video game.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for a video game in which several people play at once.

clue.text: Crow drew in another bird when temperature dropped

indicators.note: in means the sketching word is placed inside the bird
dropped means the temperature letter falls out of the bird's name

parts.note: a cockatoo is a crested parrot
to doodle is to draw idly

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher sketched a crow and another bird when the weather turned cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped' takes T out of COCKATOO, leaving COCKAOO for DOODLED to go into.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockerel's crow is written as this noise, so the call stands for the crowing.

clue.text: Travel quickly back and forth, discovering what's out there

indicators.note: back means the travelling word is read in reverse

parts.note: to speed is to travel quickly
to pace is to walk forth with measured steps

explanation.surface: Travelling back and forth fast, discovering what lies beyond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back and forth' reads as one phrase but is split: 'back' is the reversal signal, while 'forth' supplies the stepping word.
explanation.definitionFit: The far reaches of the universe beyond our solar system lie out there, beyond Earth.

clue.text: Turner song about exploitation

indicators.note: about means the song word goes around the exploitation word

parts.note: a carol is a song
use is exploitation of something

explanation.surface: A song by a Turner (Tina?) about exploitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' suggests the painter or singer, but it is simply something that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: A merry-go-round rotates, so it is a thing that turns.

clue.text: Shaman initiates journeying, dropping a variety of drugs

definitions.note: a class of drugs, given as a plural

indicators.note: journeying means the letters travel about into a new order
dropping means the letters of a are left out of the fodder

explanation.surface: A shaman's novices go on a spirit journey, giving up assorted drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of SHAMAN INITIATES, less one A, are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: These medicines, used against allergies like hay fever, are one class of pharmaceuticals.

clue.text: Snap swell of tide — what are the odds?

indicators.note: the odds are the odd-numbered letters, so the first, third, fifth and so on are taken

explanation.surface: Snapping a photo of a tidal swell, a long-shot chance.
explanation.definitionFit: A snap is a photograph, and this one is a self-portrait taken on a phone.

clue.text: Mix a large gin, for starters, in the mornings

indicators.note: in means the opening letters go inside the mornings

parts.note: AM is the abbreviation for morning, so two mornings give AM twice

indicators.note: for starters means taking the first letter of each of a, large and gin

explanation.surface: Mixing a large gin first thing every morning.
explanation.definitionFit: An amalgam is a blend or mixture of different things.

clue.text: Concerned with class — that's unusual in a lord

definitions.note: an adjective: relating to an order, a classification in biology

indicators.note: unusual means the letters are arranged in an uncommon way

explanation.surface: Talking about social class, which is odd for an aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: In taxonomy the word describes something relating to an order, a rank in classification.

clue.text: Dress in mirror after seeing doctor

indicators.note: after seeing means the mirror word comes after the doctor

parts.note: to ape is to mirror or imitate

explanation.surface: Getting dressed in front of a mirror after visiting the doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: To drape is to dress or cover in loosely hung cloth.

clue.text: Sea salt eroded navigational aids

indicators.note: eroded means the letters are worn away and remade in another order

explanation.surface: Salty sea spray has worn away the sailors' charts.
explanation.definitionFit: Books of maps are used by travellers to find their way.

clue.text: Comeback of star is hollow

indicators.note: comeback suggests going back, so the words are read in reverse

parts.note: the sun is a star

explanation.surface: A celebrity's comeback rings hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinus is a hollow cavity, especially within the bones of the face.

clue.text: Uncoordinated fake jewellery

parts.note: a sham is a fake
bling is slang for showy jewellery

explanation.surface: Cheap fake jewellery that doesn't match.
explanation.definitionFit: A shambling gait is awkward and clumsy, lacking coordination.

clue.text: Tree bark

definitions.meaning: to bark or howl like a hound

explanation.definitionFit: The laurel tree has this name, and a hound's deep howling is also called it.

clue.text: Long story entertains beginning to end

indicators.note: a host entertains guests inside, so the story word holds the letter

parts.note: a yarn is a tale

indicators.note: beginning to means only the first letter of end is taken

explanation.surface: A long story keeps you entertained from start to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective describing the story but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to want it badly, to pine.

clue.text: Wary when left with spooky sound

indicators.note: sound means the spooky word is said aloud and written as it is heard

parts.note: eerie means spooky

explanation.surface: Someone left alone becomes wary on hearing a spooky noise.
explanation.definitionFit: To be leery is to be suspicious and cautious of something.

clue.text: Grooms animal within bounds of stables

indicators.note: within means the animal is placed inside the two letters
the bounds of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: a marten is a weasel-like animal

explanation.surface: A stable hand grooms a horse inside the stables.
explanation.definitionFit: To groom is to tidy or spruce up, and smartens is the same verb form.
